subject: SLA alignment: uptime bands & maintenance window scoping for Finexa
messages:
From: Dana Moore <dana.moore@finexa.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@finexa.com
Date: 2027-05-20T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: SLA proposal – maintenance window requirements and credit calculation

Kimberly / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move towards contracting, Finexa needs to align on two items before our procurement/legal teams will sign: uptime measurement bands for our public inference endpoints, and a defined maintenance window policy that won’t disrupt our nightly settlement pipeline (runs 02:00–04:30 ET).

Our asks:
- A hard uptime target for customer-facing inference endpoints, with a predictable monthly credit schedule we can model in our TCO. We're proposing 99.5% as the baseline for the hosted plan for now.
- Guaranteed maintenance windows: we need at least one predictable weekly maintenance window that can be scheduled outside our settlement window, and for rare urgent maintenance events we request a 72-hour notice or compensating credit if it impacts our 02:00–05:00 ET window.

We recognize Redwood’s standard terms; we’re asking for a narrow amendment scoped to our account (FNX-4387) rather than a global change. Attached is a short CSV with our batch window times and a one-page sketch of how Finexa would like monthly credit calculations to appear in invoices.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: (a) offer a scoped uptime band (either 99.5% or a split policy where core routes are 99.9% and batch routes are 99.5%) and (b) put maintenance scheduling commitments into the order form?

Goal: get to a mutually agreeable SLA amendment we can sign by June 3.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

—Dana Moore
Director of Ops, Finexa
Dana.Moore@finexa.com
attachments: maintenance-window-schedule.csv
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Dana Moore <dana.moore@finexa.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-20T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA proposal – maintenance window requirements and credit calculation

Dana —

Thanks for the clear ask and for the schedule CSV; that helped. We appreciate Finexa scoping this to FNX-4387. A few quick notes from Redwood’s side so we can keep the conversation narrow and actionable:

1) Uptime bands: our hosted default is measured at the API-gateway level and is 99.9% monthly for production routes. We can be flexible on subset scoping ("core" vs "background ingestion" endpoints). For a split policy we’d propose:
   - Core endpoints (payment validation, live inference): 99.9% monthly
   - Background ingestion / batch-only routes: 99.7% monthly

2) Credit calculation: Redwood uses a graduated monthly credit matrix (percent of monthly invoice) tied to minutes of unavailable time. We can map that to the CSV you sent and provide a worked example for your invoicing team. As an accommodation, for FNX-4387 we can floor the credit at a minimum of $X (we’ll propose numbers in the draft).

3) Maintenance windows: we want to avoid hard blackouts for engineering velocity, but we can commit to a primary weekly maintenance window outside your settlement window and to provide 72-hour notice for planned maintenance that might affect your 02:00–05:00 ET window. For emergency maintenance we’d keep the standard notification + post-incident report; if an emergency event affects your settlement window we can offer a one-off credit or make good on capacity while we remediate.

I’m looping in Ben (pricing) and Laura (contracts) to draft a small amendment/wording that we can sign as an order addendum. Marcus has a redline she could propose — Marcus, can you take the CSV and sketch a short amendment and a credit table that maps to Finexa’s example?

If helpful, we can do a 30-min sync tomorrow morning (PST).

Best,

Kimberly Park
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123
redwood.ai
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, Dana Moore <dana.moore@finexa.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-21T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA proposal – redline + proposed maintenance scoping

Kimberly / Dana —

Attaching a concise redline and a draft amendment for the order (redwood-sla-redline.docx and redwood-sla-amendment-draft.pdf). Key items I adjusted vs. the standard template:

- Measured Scope: explicitly enumerates "core inference" (payment, auth, low-latency scoring) vs. "batch ingestion" endpoints and ties measurement to API route tags.
- Uptime thresholds: 99.9% for core, 99.7% for batch ingestion (we landed on 99.7 after modeling your CSV and the historic window overlap).
- Maintenance carveouts: Planned maintenance is limited to one weekly 3-hour window (customer-selectable) and we provide a 72-hour scheduled notice for anything outside that window. Planned maintenance affecting the settlement window (02:00–05:00 ET) requires either rescheduling or a guaranteed compensating credit equal to 5% of that day’s pro-rata daily charges for the impacted service segment.
- Emergency events: emergency maintenance remains carveouts only for true security or data integrity events; otherwise we treat them as measured downtime for credits.

I also included a worked numeric example on page 3 showing how a 99.7% vs 99.9% threshold maps to minutes and to % credits on your sample monthly invoice. If this wording looks good, I’ll convert to a DocuSign-ready addendum and include the maintenance-window-schedule.csv as an exhibit.

Notes / open items:
- Pricing commit: Ben — we’ll need to confirm the minimum credit floor and whether we offer a separate monthly resilience credit bucket in the order.
- Sign-off: Kimberly — once you and Dana confirm, I’ll publish the DocuSign link.

—Marcus Lin
Staff Counsel, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
attachments: redwood-sla-redline.docx, redwood-sla-amendment-draft.pdf
From: Dana Moore <dana.moore@finexa.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@finexa.com, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-22T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA proposal – redline + proposed maintenance scoping

Marcus / Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the redline. The proposed split (99.9% core / 99.7% batch) plus the one weekly selectable maintenance window is acceptable to Finexa, pending two small clarifications:

1) The compensating credit for rescheduled planned maintenance that impacts our 02:00–05:00 ET settlement window — can you express that as a defined % (e.g., 5% of the pro-rata daily charges) in the addendum so our accounting team can model it (your draft suggested a mechanism but didn’t fix the number).

2) For emergency maintenance: we need a commit to a post-incident root cause analysis (RCA) within 5 business days for any event that results in credits being issued.

If you can add those two points to the DocuSign-ready addendum I think we can route for signature on our end next week. Appreciate the collaborative approach — small ask: include the worked numeric example as a cover page so legal has something to run through the invoicing model.

I’ll stand by for the DocuSign link.

—Dana
Director of Ops, Finexa
